note: Immutable P0 remains historical evidence. P2 rule migrations are append-only ledger entries loaded from migratedRuleModules, with one immutable mapping per JSON module. The manifest owns shared metadata and ordered module membership only. Verification compares the hydrated mapping set against the PR base, including legacy monolithic bases, so storage modularization cannot weaken the one-way ratchet. Only entries absent from the comparison-base state form the current transaction: a historical terminal destination may later be consumed as the source of a new mapping, while the older entry remains immutable. Contract v2 adds only a narrow append-only kind=retire transaction for ordinary unlayered P0 rules whose consumers were intentionally removed. P2-K retirement rejects layered sources, !important declarations, and custom-property declarations; those cases require a separately reviewed future contract rather than compatibility branches here. Each transaction source occurrence must exist in its declared base layer (null means unlayered), only unlayered origins reduce P0 debt, every transaction destination must be explicitly layered in the same stylesheet, declarations must be preserved losslessly with physical cascade precedence intact, and exact-selector conflicts are reviewed separately for normal and important declarations. Mapped files also retain canonical keyframe and non-layer at-rule semantics. Keyframe and runtime-style migrations remain disabled until their own contracts are implemented.
